title: Xenograft supervision and joint methylation-fragment-end encoding define a reusable molecular scoring layer for cell-free tumor DNA
abstract: Circulating tumor DNA is often scarce in plasma, and regional methylation summaries can obscure informative differences between individual molecules. Here we present ctDNA-BERT, a Transformer that scores individual bisulfite reads without predefined differentially methylated regions by jointly encoding CpG methylation state, nucleotide context and the fragment 3 ′ end. Xenografts provide molecule-level tumor supervision. The resulting frozen scorer supported tumor-fraction estimation in synthetic and patient-derived xenograft mixtures and enriched tumor-concordant methylation and chromatin-accessibility signals in independent hepatocellular carcinoma and stage III pan-cancer plasma without cohort-specific retraining. Features derived from selected reads discriminated stage I cancers from healthy controls in a retrospective cohort of 1,477 specimens, achieving an out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.884. By separating molecular scoring from sample-level inference, ctDNABERT provides a reusable read-level scoring layer for cell-free DNA methylation analysis.
